**Classification note:** the incident is logged as "0 people at risk," but the log itself reports 85 attendees mid-session (60 main_stage, 25 workshop_room) with badge-reader doors failed open. Treat occupant safety and life-safety-egress as live concerns, not a zero-risk IT event.

# Burning Electrical Smell? 6 Safety Steps to Take Right Away
A burning electrical smell almost always points to overheating, arcing, or scorched insulation, and it belongs in the “treat it as a possible fire” category until proven otherwise. If you see smoke or flame, get everyone out and call 911. If there’s no visible fire, keep people away from the area, switch off the affected circuit if you can do it safely, and call a professional right away. > - Sustained sparking, rapidly rising heat, or a wall or panel hot to the touch warrants evacuation and a 911 call from outside. ## What to Do in the First Few Minutes After You Smell Burning
1. Evacuate immediately if you see smoke, flame, hear sustained sparking, or notice heat rising quickly near a wall, outlet, or panel, and call 911 from outside the home.

# Burning Electrical Smell? 6 Safety Steps to Take Right Away
A burning electrical smell almost always points to overheating, arcing, or scorched insulation, and it belongs in the “treat it as a possible fire” category until proven otherwise. If you see smoke or flame, get everyone out and call 911. If there’s no visible fire, keep people away from the area, switch off the affected circuit if you can do it safely, and call a professional right away. > - Sustained sparking, rapidly rising heat, or a wall or panel hot to the touch warrants evacuation and a 911 call from outside. ## What to Do in the First Few Minutes After You Smell Burning
1. Evacuate immediately if you see smoke, flame, hear sustained sparking, or notice heat rising quickly near a wall, outlet, or panel, and call 911 from outside the home.
